title: Sell Mineral Rights in Cecil-Bishop, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Cecil-Bishop, PA | Southpointe
metaDescription: Cecil-Bishop mineral owners near Southpointe: get a clear cash offer on your Marcellus royalty interest, explained plainly, no pressure.
heroLead: Cecil Township is home to Southpointe, the business park where Range Resources built its headquarters, which makes this one of the more closely watched corners of Washington County's gas business.
intro: If your family holds minerals in or around Cecil-Bishop, you own ground close to the heart of Marcellus operations in this state. Southpointe, the business park that anchors this township, is where Range Resources set up its headquarters as it built out the leasehold that made this county one of the most drilled in Pennsylvania. That kind of proximity to operator infrastructure doesn't automatically mean your interest is worth more, but it usually means there's a real, traceable production history behind your royalty check.
We know what it's like to hold a family interest and not fully understand what's driving the number on your statement. That's exactly the gap we try to close before talking value.

sections.heading: Ground zero for Washington County development
paragraphs: Cecil Township and the surrounding area have seen some of the county's earliest and most sustained Marcellus development, going back to the original wave of leasing in the mid-2000s. Wells here are typically well into their production life, meaning the initial steep decline curve most Marcellus wells show in their first few years has usually leveled out by now into a slower, more predictable tail.

This is squarely wet-gas country, with a meaningful natural gas liquids component in most production, which drives both the total value of the gas and the size of the post-production deduction on your statement.

sections.heading: A mature well isn't a worthless one
paragraphs: Owners sometimes assume that once a well is a decade or more into production, their mineral interest has lost most of its value. In reality, a mature, stable-decline well can be easier to price accurately than a brand-new one, because there's real history to work from instead of a projection.

sections.heading: Confirming your interest before we talk numbers
paragraphs: We trace title through the Washington County Recorder of Deeds, confirm your decimal interest against the applicable unit, and review your recent statements so the offer reflects your actual production history, not a rough estimate.

faqs.question: Does living near Range Resources' headquarters change my royalty rights?
faqs.answer: No. Proximity to a company office doesn't affect your lease terms or royalty; those are determined by your specific lease and unit.

faqs.question: My well has been producing for over ten years. Is it still worth selling?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Mature wells with a stable decline curve can be priced with real confidence, which sometimes makes them easier to value than newer wells.

faqs.question: What if my interest spans both Cecil and an adjoining township?
faqs.answer: We handle multi-township interests the same way, tracing title and unit participation for each portion before combining them into one offer.
